findings.title: Wrong-unit guard only detects an idle clock faster than microseconds
findings.why_it_matters: The intent and the shipped docs promise that a wrong idle-clock unit renders `--`; the arithmetic only catches a unit that makes the idle counter advance faster than wall time. Every check is one-sided: `if (idle > elapsed + slack) return CPU_CORE_UNKNOWN`. If the value is a coarser unit (milliseconds, seconds, a clock tick larger than 1 us), each per-core delta is a small fraction of elapsed, `busy` lands at 99.9-100 %, and CORE prints a flat 100 % on an idle console instead of `--` - the exact static-100 % failure the hardware checklist warns about, and indistinguishable from a genuinely saturated machine. The b153 hardware run is specifically meant to settle whether the microsecond assumption holds, and on the wrong outcome the panel would confidently show a fabricated number rather than failing closed.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one and make code and docs agree. (a) Minimal: correct the guarantee in PROJECTS.md, DECISIONS.md D103, ARCHITECTURE.md section 7 and the metrics.c comment to say only a faster-than-microsecond idle clock is rejected, so the hardware checklist stops claiming a mismatch always renders `--`. (b) Behavioural: add a lower-bound plausibility guard - if every active core reads exactly 100 % for five consecutive windows (0.5 s), refuse the sample and render `--` until the reading drops, since this dashboard app cannot legitimately pin all four cores for half a second. Assumption: a false `--` is the safe direction under the project rule that a missing value beats a fabricated one.

findings.title: Added CPU validity mask and fake rate hook have no consumer
findings.why_it_matters: The diff adds `Metrics.cpu_active_mask`, written twice in the sampler and read nowhere, and `fake_set_cpu_activity`, declared and defined but never called. The unused setter is worse for coverage: it advertises that the rate path can be driven to a chosen value, but no test ever does, so the 0/S and counter-stall cases stay unasserted. residual_risks: Catch-up sampling can feed sub-window measurements into the readout and the 20 s trace: metrics_sample_slow() is re-run up to MAX_CATCH_UP_SAMPLES (3, app.h:21) in the tight loop at app.c:501-506. The first call spans the hitch, but the following adjacent calls have an elapsed of only the few microseconds the sampler itself takes. Over that window one running core can show a genuine 0 us idle delta (100 %) and a single context switch turns into a five-figure CTX rate, so after a >200 ms stall (for example a config commit on the main thread) CORE can flash an arbitrary average and rate for one tick and record that sample in a 20 s trace whose axis assumes 100 ms samples. Host tests and the fake (fixed 100 ms step) cannot reproduce it; hardware has not been observed.

The aggregate in sample_cpu averages the raw idle delta (metrics.c:157), while cpu_pct_from_idle clamps its by-value copy to elapsed at metrics.c:90. In the slack band (idle slightly above elapsed) the per-core value is a clamped 0 % but the aggregate still subtracts the overshoot, so the average can read below the displayed cores by up to the slack (~0.5 points per fully idle core at 10 Hz). Bounded and cosmetic, but the two paths should use the same clamped delta.

findings.title: Idle-clock unit guard is one-sided but documented as fail-closed
findings.why_it_matters: If `cpuInfo[].idleClock` is not microseconds on this console, CORE does not fall back to `--`. A counter that advances more slowly than wall time (milliseconds, seconds) passes the `idle > elapsed` check, and the ratio then renders a permanent ~100 %, which is the exact fabricated number D6/D103 forbid and the exact symptom PROJECT.md's hardware checklist says must never appear. The workspace rule is that a value the platform cannot supply renders `--`, never a guess, and the stated intent for this change was to fail closed on a wrong unit; only one direction of unit error is detected. The four comments and docs that promise a full guarantee must be corrected to the one-sided guarantee and the slower-unit symptom added to the hardware checklist, or the guard must gain a second direction.

findings.title: CTX/WAKE print a fabricated 0/S when the cumulative delta regresses

findings.title: Refused CPU rate deltas render as measured 0/S
findings.why_it_matters: CORE prints `CTX 0/S  WAKE 0/S` as if it had measured them whenever the CPU sample is otherwise valid. sample_cpu() zeroes both rates at the top of every sample and then silently skips the assignment when a cumulative counter goes backwards (a 32-bit `threadSwitchCount`/`comesOutOfIdleCount` wrap, or an active-mask change that shrinks the adapter's sum). Nothing clears `cpu_valid`, so panels/core.c's caption prints the untouched zero. That is exactly the fabricated number AGENTS.md rule 6 and this project's own rule forbid: a value that could not be obtained must render `--`. The fix mirrors the existing per-core handling, where absence is carried by a sentinel rather than by the zero value.

findings.title: metrics_sample_slow() contract comment omits CPU
findings.why_it_matters: The header contract still says a slow sample reads "Memory, storage, power, identity, wall clock", but the diff made CPU load — now the hero number — the sixth reading. findings.title: Unused fake_set_cpu_activity() test setter
findings.why_it_matters: The fake gains a public setter that no test or preview calls; the rate assertions in test_cpu_usage silently rely on the cpu_reset() defaults of 840 and 230 instead. An unused knob on the test port is a second place the rate policy can drift from, and it hides the fact that the asserted rates are defaults rather than the thing under test.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete fake_set_cpu_activity() from fake_platform.h and fake_platform.c, or make it the only source of the tested rates: call `fake_set_cpu_activity(900, 250)` at the top of test_cpu_usage() and assert 900/250 so the test states its own input.

findings.title: Duplicate percent rounding and clamp in metrics.c
findings.why_it_matters: The rule "round the busy fraction to nearest, then clamp to 0-100" is written twice in one file: once in cpu_pct_from_idle() and again inline for the active-core average. The two copies must be kept in step by hand, and the file already carries the sentinel, the slack guard, and the rate cap around them, so a reader has to compare both blocks to know every percentage is produced the same way. One helper deletes six lines and gives the percentage domain a single home.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract `static int cpu_clamp_pct(double busy)` holding `(int)(busy + 0.5)` plus the 0/100 clamp, and call it from cpu_pct_from_idle() (line 94) and from the aggregate branch (line 165).

residual_risks: PLATFORM_CPU_COUNT (4) mirrors the SDK's SceKernelSystemInfo.cpuInfo[4] with no static assertion, and platform_read_cpu() loops the port constant over the SDK array (platform_psp2.c:186). A future bump to the port count would read past the struct; `_Static_assert(sizeof(info.cpuInfo)/sizeof(info.cpuInfo[0]) == PLATFORM_CPU_COUNT, ...)` in the adapter would pin it.

The `cpu_active_mask` and `fake_set_cpu_activity` unused-symbol claims were established with text search only (callsite completeness: grep-only); a macro-generated or build-time reference would not appear.

The CPU percentages depend on the [C] microsecond idle-clock unit. If the unit is wrong the panel degrades to a permanently blank CPU row rather than a wrong number, which is the intended failure but is only discoverable on the pending b153 console run.
testing_gaps: No test drives a backwards rate delta (32-bit counter wrap or a shrinking active mask), so the 0/S path at metrics.c:178-183 is unasserted in either direction.

No test covers recovery after a failed CPU read. test_cpu_failed_read_leaves_trace_alone stops at the failure, so the two-window blank that follows a cleared baseline is unpinned and a regression that never resumes the trace would pass.

No test exercises the mixed case where one core's idle delta goes backwards while others remain usable (metrics.c:147), so the average-over-a-subset branch and the mask recorded for it are unexercised.

findings.title: Fabricated 0/S when scheduler counters are absent or roll back
findings.why_it_matters: When the console's cumulative switch/wakeup counters are zero-filled, frozen, or step backwards, CORE still prints a confident `CTX 0/S  WAKE 0/S`: `cpu_valid` is decided by the idle clocks alone, and the rate fields are zeroed before the delta test, so a failed counter is indistinguishable from a measured zero. On a running Vita zero context switches per second is impossible, so the hero panel shows an invented number — the exact zero-substitution the project rule forbids. The backwards step is guaranteed eventually for the 32-bit per-core counters (they wrap independently, so the four-core sum always dips), and the persistent version is the firmware partial-fill case the struct's [C] tag already worries about. A per-rate validity flag, cleared on a backwards step and set only after a positive advance, lets the caption render `--`; the adapter can mirror its existing `have_idle` idiom.
evidence: vita-cockpit/src/core/metrics.c:178 -- if (in.ctx_switches >= s_prev_cpu.ctx_switches) g_metrics.cpu_ctx_per_s = cpu_rate(in.ctx_switches - s_prev_cpu.ctx_switches, elapsed); -- an unchanged counter passes the test and yields a delta of 0, i.e. a measured-looking 0/s.

vita-cockpit/src/core/metrics.c:122-123 -- `g_metrics.cpu_ctx_per_s = 0;` / `g_metrics.cpu_wake_per_s = 0;` are re-seeded every sample, so the value left behind by a rejected delta is a plausible zero rather than an absent value.

vita-cockpit/src/panels/core.c:88-92 -- `if (g_metrics.cpu_valid) { snprintf(right, sizeof(right), "CTX %d/S  WAKE %d/S", g_metrics.cpu_ctx_per_s, g_metrics.cpu_wake_per_s); }` -- the caption's only validity gate is `cpu_valid`, which is set by idle-clock survival, not by rate survival.

vita-cockpit/src/platform/platform_psp2.c:192-207 -- `out->ctx_switches += info.cpuInfo[i].threadSwitchCount;` then `if (!have_idle) return; out->ok = 1;` -- `ok` requires only a nonzero idle clock, so zero-filled or frozen count fields still produce a sample the policy treats as valid.
README.md:194 -- "A number the platform cannot report renders `--`; it is never guessed or substituted with zero."
vita-cockpit/docs/DECISIONS.md:1997 -- the fail-closed promise names the idle-clock unit and `activeCpuMask`, but not the two cumulative rate counters the intent also says must fail closed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add per-rate validity to Metrics (e.g. `cpu_ctx_valid` / `cpu_wake_valid`): set each when a forward delta is measured, clear it on a backwards step or while the cumulative value has never advanced, and have `draw_caption` render THEME_ABSENT for a rate whose flag is clear. Optionally mirror the `have_idle` gate in `platform_read_cpu` with a `have_counters` check if a fully absent pair should blank the whole row. Add zero, unchanged, and backwards-counter cases to tools/test/test_metrics.c.

residual_risks: The unit guard is one-directional. `core/metrics.c:82` rejects only `idle > elapsed + slack`; if the 3.65 `idleClock` is coarser than microseconds (milliseconds, or a kHz tick), a fully idle core's delta is a small fraction of `elapsed`, every core reads ~100 %, and the trace pins to the top. That is the 'static 100 %' the hardware checklist warns about, while D103 claims a unit mismatch cannot become a percentage. The fake and the tests only exercise the finer-unit direction or an exact 2x mismatch.

There is no upper bound on `elapsed`. A multi-second gap (LiveArea/standby, debugger pause, a long stall) is averaged as if it were one 100 ms window. If `sceKernelGetProcessTimeWide` advances across standby while `idleClock` does not (or the reverse), the first post-resume sample is a fabricated ~100 % that is pushed into the trace, or a rejected sample that blanks the row for two windows.

`sceKernelGetSystemInfo` is a strong SceLibKernel import, so a missing NID on 3.65 fails at module load instead of degrading to `--`. The repo's own b141 SceNet failure (agent-wiki/13-fact-check.md) is the precedent. The [C] tag documents the risk, but 'fail closed' cannot cover an unresolved import.

Catch-up burst: app.c:501-505 can run `metrics_sample_slow()` up to MAX_CATCH_UP_SAMPLES (app.h:21) times inside one frame, so the few milliseconds between those calls becomes a full CPU sample. The extra samples use a window that can fall below the 2 ms slack floor, compress the trace's 20 s time base, and can print a short-window CTX/WAKE rate; the policy has no minimum-window rejection.
testing_gaps: No test calls `metrics_sample_slow()` twice back-to-back (the app's catch-up path). The fake advances exactly 100 ms per call, so the short-window percentage and rate paths are never exercised.
No test covers zero, unchanged, or backwards `ctx_switches` / `wakeups` -- the case that currently renders `CTX 0/S` on the panel.

No test exercises an idle delta inside the slack band (`elapsed < idle <= elapsed + slack`), so the clamp-to-zero branch in `cpu_pct_from_idle` and the unclamped value it contributes to `idle_sum` are untested; the only unit test uses a 2x mismatch.

The memory failed-read path lost its assertion: `test_failed_memory_leaves_trace_alone` was replaced by the CPU equivalent, and test_metrics.c now calls `fake_set_memory_absent()` only through `test_alert_policy`, so nothing asserts `mem_valid == 0` or the three pools rendering `--` after a failed read.
No test changes `activeCpuMask` between samples, so a core appearing or disappearing and the mask-intersection behaviour are unverified.
